summary:
**The Silent Explorers Museum** is an interactive digital museum designed to introduce children and young people to the stories of spacecraft that have completed their missions but left a lasting legacy in humanity's exploration of space.

Visitors can explore the Moon and Mars galleries and discover five pioneering explorers: the Apollo 11 Eagle Lunar Module descent stage, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity. Each exhibit presents authentic photographs, mission details, scientific contributions, and historical milestones. Through fictional first-person storytelling, the spacecraft introduce themselves, while an optional audio feature allows visitors to listen to their stories. Quizzes, achievement badges, and a participation certificate further enrich the learning experience.

Our project brings attention to historic missions that are often overlooked in favor of currently active space missions. By combining NASA-based information with storytelling and interactive learning, we make space exploration more accessible and engaging. We believe that when a mission ends, the knowledge and inspiration it leaves behind should never be forgotten.
details:
The Silent Explorers Museum is an interactive digital learning experience designed to introduce children and young people to the scientific legacy of spacecraft whose missions have come to an end.

The project is organized into two main galleries: the Moon and Mars. Visitors can explore the Apollo 11 Eagle Lunar Module's descent stage, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity. Each exhibit presents mission information, major discoveries, scientific contributions, historical details, and visual storytelling. The spacecraft tell their stories through fictional first-person narratives, which are clearly distinguished from scientific facts. Visitors can also listen to these stories through an optional audio introduction feature. An interactive quiz, achievement badges, and a participation certificate make the learning experience more engaging. A digital storybook and a presentation for the jury further support the project's educational and outreach goals.

The main benefit of our project is that it draws attention not only to the beginnings and achievements of space missions, but also to the scientific contributions they leave behind after their missions end. Visitors learn what these spacecraft accomplished, how scientific discoveries are made, and why these missions matter to humanity. Our project aims to encourage curiosity, increase scientific awareness, and inspire a greater interest in space exploration.

The museum was developed as a web-based project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its audio introduction feature includes a separate MP3 recording for each spacecraft, which visitors can play whenever they wish. If an MP3 file cannot be played, the browser's built-in text-to-speech technology serves as a fallback. The educational content is based primarily on official NASA mission pages and scientific resources. AI tools were used to support the development process, and the scientific information was also reviewed for accuracy. No specialized hardware is required; the museum can be accessed using a computer or mobile device with a web browser.

The creative aspect of our project lies in presenting retired spacecraft not simply as historical objects, but as silent explorers sharing their own stories. By combining scientific information with storytelling, audio introductions, and gamification, the museum goes beyond traditional ways of presenting information.

Throughout development, our team considered the age of the target audience, scientific accuracy, ease of use, clear language, visual appeal, and accessibility across different devices. Our goal is not only to teach children about space exploration, but also to encourage them to become Guardians of Memory who preserve and share the legacy of these missions.
